subject: Civil Engineering
title: Prestressed Concrete
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prestressed Concrete.

hook.text: Squeeze concrete before loading it and it can span farther than any regular beam.

buildup.text: High-strength steel tendons are stretched tight and anchored — they compress the concrete.

discovery.text: Pre-tensioning stretches tendons before pouring. Post-tensioning threads them after curing.

twist.text: The compression offsets tension from loads — the concrete never feels tension at all.

climax.text: Prestressed girders span 150+ feet — highway bridges use them as standard components.

punchline.text: Put the squeeze on concrete before loading it, and it goes the extra distance.

quiz.question: What is the difference between pre-tensioning and post-tensioning?
options: Pre-tensioning uses steel cables; post-tensioning uses fiberglass
Pre-tensioning stretches tendons before pouring; post-tensioning does it after curing
Pre-tensioning is for beams; post-tensioning is only for columns

details.summary: Prestressed concrete is compressed by steel tendons before loads are applied, so the concrete starts in compression and must be pulled into tension before it can crack. This allows longer spans, thinner sections, and crack-free performance compared to ordinary reinforced concrete.
details.whyItMatters: Prestressing enables concrete to span distances and carry loads impossible with ordinary reinforcement. Most modern bridge girders, parking structures, and high-rise floor systems use prestressed concrete.
takeaways: Pre-tensioning stretches tendons before concrete is cast around them
Post-tensioning stretches tendons after the concrete has hardened
Prestressed members can span 30 to 50 percent farther than reinforced ones

faq.question: What is the difference between pre-tensioning and post-tensioning?
faq.answer: In pre-tensioning, steel strands are stretched between abutments in a factory before concrete is poured around them. When concrete hardens, strands are cut and their recoil force compresses the concrete.

faq.question: Why does pre-compressing concrete prevent cracking under load?
faq.answer: Applied loads create tension in the bottom of beams. Prestressing creates compression in that same zone. The applied tension must first overcome the prestress compression before the concrete experiences net tension.
